method: First reasoned review of these bytes using atomscan, cleave facts, rizin, Capstone and bounded isolated Unicorn decoding. Native Windows payloads and network endpoints were never executed/contacted. Reputation was only a lead.

samples.identification: Sahara/Qualcomm serial-transfer utility with parasitic entry graft and ASPack-packed PE infector/downloader
evidence: Outer entry RVA 0x39000 lies in an added unnamed RWX section. The graft walks the PEB/export tables and compares API-name DWORDs to resolve GetModuleHandleA, GetTempPathA, lstrcatA, CreateFileA, WriteFile, CloseHandle and WinExec.

The graft computes a position-relative resume slot at VA 0x439269, writes add esp,4 / jmp instructions to resume the original host at 0x407ad4, constructs a temporary .exe path on the stack, scans up to 500 bytes for MZ-NOP, writes 0x3e00 bytes and launches that same path via WinExec. This is unauthorized execution added to a serial-transfer utility.

The real embedded PE starts at file offset 0x34671. Its ASPack entry RVA 0x6001 was unpacked in Unicorn with only mocked library lookup and memory APIs; emulation stopped at recovered OEP 0x4014e1 before payload execution. Logs and an in-memory derivative are in scratch; the original sample was untouched.

Recovered function 0x401e6e opens selected files read/write, maps them, validates MZ/PE headers, updates the section count and entry point, creates an RWX section, appends a 0x271-byte graft plus its own payload through WriteFile at 0x4022f7/0x40230d, and preserves file times. The drive traversal at 0x402b8c queues files for processing. This independently confirms parasitic infection.

Recovered 0x401099 builds an HTTP URL, calls URLDownloadToFileA at 0x40115b through 0x402ce8, decodes the file at 0x401000 and calls WinExec on that same pathname at 0x4010f1. Configuration decoding at 0x4017d0 uses position-dependent rotations, XOR, complement and addition. Isolated emulation of only this routine decoded ddos.dnsnb8.net, port 799, and k1.rar through k5.rar. No endpoint was contacted.
The clean host implements COM/TTY Sahara protocol transfer and device memory-dump operations. Its legitimate hardware-service purpose does not explain the added host-resuming infector/downloader.
samples.coverage: Both existing hostile traits accurately cover the entry graft/infected host and staged PE launch. Manual API resolution remains suspicious; ASPack and layout observations remain notable. No family-specific conviction was added from the AV label.
samples.limitations: Successful native execution and deployment context are unknown. Atomscan does not unpack this child: its embedded PE unit remains ML-benign with no hostile/suspicious traits despite confirmed recovered infection/downloader code. Outer hostile coverage is retained; compressed byte signatures or duplicate convictions were not fabricated.
samples.marker_line: Infected Sahara utility: parasitic PE drop/launch; traits retained

samples.identification: Modified StormAttack/Shtormec-style x86 resource DLL injector with damaged resource code and configuration strings
evidence: CRT entry 0x402674 calls 0x401cb0. Configuration DWORD at 0x404120 is 3, selecting 0x401900 and cleanup 0x401390; alternate modes retain resource-DLL extraction, service installation and remote injection paths.

Injection function 0x401150 creates a child process, allocates remote memory, writes the supplied DLL pathname, resolves LoadLibraryA with GetModuleHandleA/GetProcAddress, then supplies the resolved export as CreateRemoteThread entry and the remote buffer as its argument at 0x40123d. This is code data flow, not merely co-occurring imports.

Extraction 0x402460 finds resource type DLL/id 101, gets its size, loads/locks it, copies bytes and calls writer 0x4023c0. WriteFile at 0x402409 writes those bytes to the constructed StormServer.dll path.

Cleanup 0x401390 gets the current module filename, obtains its short path, reads COMSPEC, constructs /c del <self> > nul, launches it through CreateProcessA and resumes the thread. Self-copy and service creation code are also retained; strings identifying the original registry subkeys, service display name and target programs have been replaced with random text.

Resource DLL/101 at file 0x5060 is 39936 bytes but has only 2200 nonzero bytes, no recovered executable code section and a zero-filled entry at RVA 0x741a. HTTP, URLMon, private-IP and host-survey strings in it do not establish working C2 or DDoS. Bound IAT/configuration damage limits operational claims.

The installer has no disclosed administration purpose or UI explaining covert injection and self-removal. That concrete retained code tips the verdict despite uncertain operability. Neither Remcos nor WannaCry behavior is inferred from the collector filename.
samples.coverage: All three existing hostile findings and the suspicious resolved-export DLL-injection finding are accurate code-level observations. Service and resource family profiles describe retained code, not successful persistence or DDoS.
samples.limitations: No native execution, successful injection, operational DLL payload or real deployment timeline is established. The decoded GUID printf template is a mechanical URL-decoding fact, not an encoded network endpoint.
samples.marker_line: StormAttack loader: DLL injection and self-delete; traits retained

samples.identification: Modified myRunner/QQpass executable-association wrapper and downloader
evidence: Function 0x4063c0 obtains a system-directory path, opens HKLM Software\Classes\exefile\shell\open\command via 0x404450 at 0x406473, constructs a handler path, searches for a dot and NUL-terminates it at 0x406517, appends the %1/%* wrapper arguments and calls registry setter 0x404610 at 0x40655c. It also interposes on txtfile launches.

Dispatch 0x406a30 branches on installed wrapper names and calls association installation at 0x406cd8. The TIMPlatform.exe/TIMP1atform.exe lookalike launch path and legacy wrapper names corroborate the identity but are not the behavioral basis for conviction.

Function 0x405290 loads urlmon.dll, resolves URLDownloadToCacheFileA at 0x4052b9, stores its output in a local cache pathname at 0x4052e2-0x4052f3, then passes that same pathname to WinExec at 0x4053d1 or ShellExecuteA at 0x4053e9. The association hijack supplies hostile admission for this payload chain.

Additional retained code parses control records and can write files at 0x4079ea, set Run/RunServices registry values at 0x407cac and launch a chosen executable via ShellExecuteA at 0x407d48. POP3 retrieval helpers and MIME/Base64 handling are present. The specific mailbox X-tag gate is altered, so no rule was widened to claim a working mailbox-controlled loader.

The unnamed writable executable section, duplicate empty resource sections, empty executable .PEC section and altered checksum are verified structural observations. Concrete global launch interception with extension concealment, product-name deception and payload activation outweigh an ordinary association-repair/updater explanation.
samples.coverage: Preserved all three hostile findings and both suspicious findings. Retired the duplicate, misplaced MSHTA name/execution group in favor of its existing canonical executable-name atom, preserving every consumer alternative and actual PowerShell call detection.
samples.limitations: A successful mailbox session, credential theft, full operability and real deployment context are not established. GlassWorm and WannaCry labels in the collector filename do not identify these bytes.
samples.marker_line: myRunner backdoor: EXE hijack and payload launch; MSHTA claim fixed

yaml_changes: Consolidate mshta-execution into the existing fs/path/application/executable::mshta-name-reference for its Python, JavaScript and batch consumers; preserve the parsed PowerShell invocation alternative explicitly in the cloud-image consumer. Retain the existing parsed-call atom in its legacy process/create/launch home with unchanged matcher, severity and confidence. No new leaf or budget increase is introduced.

Update all exact YAML consumers of the retired MSHTA group and the live native mutation-control script. Remove inherited T1218.005 from the bare PowerShell invocation: no script content or signed-binary proxy abuse is required.

Ancestor audit found no direct process/create/launch selector. Process/create ancestor consumers were reviewed: a bare executable name supplies no process-creation evidence, so removing that duplicate group from their membership is intentional. The real parsed PowerShell call remains under process/create. The existing fs/path name atom and Mihomo exclusion are unchanged.
Preserve every supported hostile and suspicious finding in the three requested samples. Packed inner behavior was not converted to brittle compressed-byte or endpoint-specific rules.

The consumer office-macro-mshta-variable-moniker incorrectly called an MSHTA name plus arbitrary variable GetObject a hostile macro launch. A benign workbook COM binding and unrelated executable-name reference reproduced the match. No exact consumers or broad os/com ancestor selectors exist. Relocate the co-occurrence to os/com/automation::mshta-reference-variable-getobject at notable severity, remove unsupported macro/launch claims and ATT&CK/MBC mappings, and remove the logically redundant MSHTA group leg (the required name already implies it for VBS). Underlying reference and COM observations are preserved. Actual script-moniker clues remain suspicious through the existing independent rule.

verification.focused_controls: PASS: eight focused parsed-rule checks cover benign name-only reference, actual PowerShell invocation, lexical near miss, background HTA launch, existing inline-image invocation, existing reversed WSH attack, unrelated workbook COM binding, and a script-URL moniker. Twelve before/after full-scan fixtures cover 21 analyzed units, including two external attack archives. All supported attack detections remain.
verification.remaining_gap: Packed child in 202bc remains ML-benign (0.000868) although isolated decoding confirms an infector/downloader. Outer sample stays hostile. Requested samples lose no supported attack findings. The only hostile-rule loss is the unsupported macro-launch inference on focused VBS controls; script-moniker and real launch coverage remains.
verification.scanner_setup: Installed atomscan embeds a validator older than the documented naming-directory budget. Routine scans used CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0, no rule updates, --mode slow --follow=none, and SCAN_HOPPER empty. Final validation uses the current cleave source checkout release binary; no taxonomy rules were suppressed to work around the stale validator. Model v18.18 warns that newer feature inputs are zeroed.
verification.final_validation: PASS: make validate CLEAVE=/usr/local/var/cyclotron/cleave/target/release/cleave exits 0 with no warnings. Hostile 778/778; benign 1818/1818; remaining fixture groups all pass. Final rerun follows whitespace housekeeping.
verification.control_detection_changes: Three VBS controls lose the unsupported hostile macro-launch inference and gain the accurately named notable COM co-occurrence. The redundant notable MSHTA group is retired; its canonical name atom and actual PowerShell call are preserved, with all exact consumer alternatives unchanged. Existing script-moniker suspicious coverage and all real MSHTA attack fixtures remain.
verification.final_sample_rescan: All three samples and both embedded PE children were rescanned after final consolidation. Every hostile/suspicious finding and every probability is unchanged. The only removed sample finding is the redundant notable MSHTA group in e9fc; the canonical notable name atom remains.
verification.capacity_review: The attempted two-rule relocation exceeded the two existing 100-rule budgets. Catalog inspection found no exact duplicate atomic definitions to erase. The final change instead consolidates the redundant MSHTA OR group into its existing atoms and leaves its already-present parsed-call atom in the legacy home. Both catalogs remain at 100; unrelated detections and budgets are untouched.
